tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Lists the projects this credential can act on. A project is one site or brand under the account, and every widget, lead, campaign and sequence belongs to one. Every other tool takes an optional project argument: pass one of these ids to run that call in that project. Without it, a call uses the conn

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Creates a project — one more site or brand under the account — and returns its id. Pass that id as the project argument on later calls to work inside it. Projects cannot be deleted from here.

tools.name: offer_choice
tools.description: Presents the user with a choice between 2 to 4 options, each with a label and a one-line description, one optionally marked recommended. It is for decisions where reasonable options would build different things — which widget kind, what score ranges, what copy or trigger — and nothing the user said

tools.name: read_plan_usage
tools.description: Reads the account's plan and what it has used of each monthly quota: leads captured, emails sent, AI messages, plus how many websites and widgets exist against the plan's limits. Leads are counted over the billing period and everything else over the calendar month (UTC). `plan` is null when no plan

tools.name: plan_site_strategy
tools.description: Gives an agent what it needs to advise on a website's lead capture: a snapshot of the website's widgets (kind, live or draft, views, completions, conversion), the six widget kinds with where each appears, and the steps to follow — read the site, ask the user questions with offer_choice, then rank 3-

tools.name: list_widgets
tools.description: Every widget in the current project, newest last. Returns summaries only — id, name, kind, type, status, article, views, completions. Use read_widget for one widget's full content.

tools.name: read_widget
tools.description: One widget in full, plus `issues` — what is still missing before it could go live. Includes its questions, quiz questions and options, quiz tiers and calculator inputs. Which of those are meaningful depends on the kind: questions for lead-magnet and survey, quiz fields for quiz, calculator inputs fo

tools.name: create_widget
tools.description: Create a widget in the current project. Six kinds: lead-magnet, popup, survey, announcement-bar, quiz, calculator. It is always created as a draft, and the result lists `issues` — what is still missing before it could go live (empty when nothing is); fix them with update_widget. Going live is a sepa

tools.name: update_widget
tools.description: Change a widget. Only the fields sent are changed, with one exception: sending ANY of questions, quizQuestions, quizTiers or calcInputs replaces ALL FOUR with exactly what is sent, so send the complete set you want to end up with. Publishing is a separate action. Views and completions cannot be set

tools.name: request_widget_publish
tools.description: Ask for a draft widget to go live. This requests publication; it does not publish. Called over the API or MCP with a key it does NOT publish: it creates a pending approval carrying a before/after snapshot and returns it, and the widget goes live only when a signed-in person approves it in the dashbo

tools.name: start_experiment
tools.description: Split traffic between a control widget and 1 to 3 variants. The variants must already exist as their own live widgets, of the same kind and project as the control (created with create_widget and made live with request_widget_publish). On a small site one variant at a time is the practical limit: eve

tools.name: stop_experiment
tools.description: End a running experiment. Counts stop with it; starting a new one on the same widgets begins with fresh counts, not a resume.

tools.name: list_leads
tools.description: Captured leads for the current project, newest first. PAGED — at most 200 per call, and the limit is a hard cap, not a default you can raise; pass offset for the next page (limit 50 with offset 50 returns leads 51 onward). These rows are real people's email addresses. Each lead carries a quality ver

tools.name: read_lead
tools.description: One lead with the answers it gave, and its quiz score and tier if it came from a quiz. The score is frozen at the moment of submission — it is what that visitor actually saw, not a recomputation against the quiz as it stands today.

tools.name: read_analytics
tools.description: Totals for the current project: widget count, page views, completions, conversion percentage, lead count and how many have unsubscribed. Conversion is completions divided by views as a whole percentage; with no views yet it reads 0, which means NO DATA rather than a failure. Completions is not leads

tools.name: list_widget_analytics
tools.description: The same numbers per widget, best-converting first. Use this to answer which magnet is working; use widget_results for where one widget's traffic came from.

tools.name: read_widget_results
tools.description: One widget's views, completions, conversion, and its leads grouped by referrer. The referrer is whatever the visitor's browser reported when they submitted, so it is a rough attribution, not a tracked source. Also returns the funnel (views, completions, leads, conversions, revenue in cents; conversi

tools.name: read_experiment_results
tools.description: The A/B experiment a widget is in (or last ran as control): per arm, assigned views, leads, conversion rate and 95% interval in basis points (1234 = 12.34%), and lift against the control arm. result "insufficient_data" means at least one arm has too few views for a rate to mean anything; in that cas

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: Campaigns in this project, newest first, with their status. Open and click numbers come from the sent-email ledger, not from a counter on the campaign.

tools.name: draft_campaign
tools.description: Create a campaign AS A DRAFT. There is no tool that sends one: sending puts mail in thousands of real inboxes, spends deliverability reputation that cannot be bought back, and cannot be undone. A person sends it from the dashboard. recipientScope is "all" or a single widget id, and unsubscribed or b

tools.name: update_campaign
tools.description: Change a draft campaign. A campaign that has already been sent cannot be edited — the ledger describes what actually went out, and editing it afterwards would make that a lie.

tools.name: list_sequences
tools.description: Sequences in this project with their steps and branch. The shape is BOUNDED: a linear chain of steps, then at most one branch point, each path its own linear chain. No nesting, no rejoining, no parallel paths.

tools.name: list_sequence_enrollments
tools.description: Who is running through which sequence: for a lead (leadId) or for a sequence (sequenceId), each enrolment's status (active, finished or stopped), the step it is on and when it is next due. This is how to answer "why did this lead get, or not get, the follow-up" — a lead with no enrolment was never e

tools.name: draft_sequence
tools.description: Create a sequence AS A DRAFT. Steps are either an email or a delay in days — a delay is its own step, so two emails can run back to back. A branch may be added at the end; its paths are evaluated first-match-wins, left to right, and a filter with field null always matches, so it only makes sense las

tools.name: update_sequence
tools.description: Change a DRAFT sequence. Only the fields sent are changed, except that sending steps or branch replaces the whole of that part, so send the complete chain you want. It cannot edit an active sequence and cannot activate one: an active sequence is paused with pause_sequence, edited, and started again

tools.name: pause_sequence
tools.description: Move a sequence to draft, which stops new enrolments. Stopping mail is never the slower path, so this applies immediately. Starting one again is activate_sequence, which a person approves: an active sequence enrols every future lead and sends on a timer with nobody watching.

tools.name: activate_sequence
tools.description: Ask for a draft sequence to start sending. Called over the API or MCP this does NOT activate it: it creates a pending approval and returns its requestId, and the sequence starts — enrolling future matching leads and mailing them on its timer — only when a signed-in person approves it in the fnlowl d

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Transactional templates in this account. Built-in starters are marked isCustom false and cannot be deleted.

tools.name: create_template
tools.description: Create a transactional template. category is one of authentication, account, orders, notifications. Use {{name}} placeholders in the subject and body for values supplied when it is sent; a placeholder nobody supplies is replaced with nothing. It creates the template only — sending needs a person.

tools.name: update_template
tools.description: Change a template's name, category, subject or body — only the fields sent. Built-in starters can be rewritten too (they just cannot be deleted). It changes what later sends of this template say; it sends nothing.

tools.name: read_brand
tools.description: The brand: site name, accent colour, sender name, logo and the postal address that every commercial email needs in its footer. With a project in scope this is that website's brand — the account defaults with the website's own overrides applied; without one it is the account defaults.

tools.name: update_brand
tools.description: Change brand settings. Only the fields sent are changed. With a project in scope this sets that website's own override and leaves the account defaults — and every other website — alone; without one it changes the account defaults every website inherits. The accent colour must be a hex value — it is

tools.name: read_ai_context
tools.description: The account's AI context: what the blog is about, its pricing tiers, value props, testimonials, design direction and tone presets. Every AI-personalised lead magnet is generated from exactly this plus the visitor's own answers. It belongs to the whole account and is shared by every website on it, so

tools.name: update_ai_context
tools.description: Change the AI context: the about text, design direction, value props, pricing tiers and testimonials that every AI-personalised lead magnet is generated from. Changes apply to generations from then on; lead magnets already sent are not rewritten. Only the fields sent are changed. It holds what the s

tools.name: read_sending_status
tools.description: Read account sending readiness, domain verification, daily usage, and recent reputation state. While the sending domain is not yet verified it also returns `records`: the DNS records to publish. `sentToday` counts the last 24 hours on a rolling basis, while `sharedTrial.sendsUsed` counts the account

tools.name: list_email_deliveries
tools.description: List recent email outcomes for this account. Recipients are masked; use this to diagnose queued, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complained, or failed mail. `sentToday` counts the last 24 hours on a rolling basis, while `sharedTrial.sendsUsed` counts the account's lifetime sends on the shared t

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description: List native integration providers and connection health. Credentials are never returned.

tools.name: read_integration_delivery_status
tools.description: Read recent queued ESP/webhook handoff outcomes and retry state. Lead identifiers, payloads, and credentials are not returned.

tools.name: read_ai_generation_status
tools.description: Read recent AI lead-magnet generation outcomes by status and widget. Visitor answers, generated content, lead ids, and failure details are not returned.

tools.name: ask_question
tools.description: Ask the fnlowl Advisor a question in plain English. It knows how fnlowl works — widgets and where each kind appears, the embed, sequences, campaigns, sending, credits, plans, MCP — and can read the account's own widgets, leads, analytics, campaigns, sequences and sending status to answer. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_plan_usage, read_widget, create_widget, update_widget, list_leads, list_campaigns, read_brand, list_email_deliveries · Private data: list_projects, create_widget, update_widget, read_sending_status, list_integrations, read_integration_delivery_status · Public sink: create_widget, update_widget, request_widget_publish, start_experiment, list_leads, list_campaigns, draft_sequence, update_sequence, read_brand, read_sending_status, list_email_deliveries, read_integration_delivery_status · Destructive: list_projects, read_widget, create_widget, update_widget, draft_sequence.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_plan_usage, read_widget, create_widget, update_widget, list_leads, list_campaigns, read_brand, list_email_deliveries · Private data: list_projects, create_widget, update_widget, read_sending_status, list_integrations, read_integration_delivery_status · Public sink: create_widget, update_widget, request_widget_publish, start_experiment, list_leads, list_campaigns, draft_sequence, update_sequence, read_brand, read_sending_status, list_email_deliveries, read_integration_delivery_status · Destructive: list_projects, read_widget, create_widget, update_widget, draft_sequence

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
